sources.shortCitation: Jones, “The Ghost of Hans J. Salter,” Cinefantastique 7, no. 2 (1978): 10
sources.fullCitation: Preston Neal Jones. “The Ghost of Hans J. Salter: The man who brought harmony to the House of Frankenstein.” Interview. Cinefantastique 7, no. 2 (Summer 1978): 10 ff. The portrait printed on page 10 is captioned “Hans J. Salter circa 1940s” and credits no photographer; the article is illustrated with excerpts from Salter’s conductor’s scores for the Universal horror films. Digitised copy at the Internet Archive. Accessed 17 August 2026.

media.title: Hans J. Salter, about 1940 — Cinefantastique, 1978
media.description: Portrait photograph of the composer Hans J. Salter, printed with Preston Neal Jones’s interview in Cinefantastique in 1978 and captioned as dating from about 1940.
media.altText: Black-and-white head-and-shoulders portrait of Hans J. Salter in a suit and tie.
media.publicCaption: Hans J. Salter in the portrait printed with Preston Neal Jones’s interview “The Ghost of Hans J. Salter” in Cinefantastique in 1978, where it is captioned “Hans J. Salter circa 1940s.” No photographer is named. Salter worked with Kaper on three films of 1933 before both reached Hollywood.
media.publicCreditLine: Photographer unidentified; Cinefantastique 7, no. 2 (Summer 1978), p. 10; digitized copy at Internet Archive.
media.rightsNote: Cinefantastique, vol. 7, no. 2 (1978), remains in copyright and the portrait carries no photographer credit or separate licence. Reuse requires permission or another applicable legal basis.
